title: Hinton's Grand Canyon test, run against an Epistemological Interface (pre-registered BEFORE building the engine)
the_original_test: Geoffrey Hinton told a chatbot 'I saw the Grand Canyon flying to Chicago.' The model attached the participle to the object and objected that the Grand Canyon is too big to fly to Chicago. Hinton corrected it -- 'No, it was me flying to Chicago' -- and the model said 'Oh, I see. I misunderstood you.' Hinton's argument: a system cannot MISunderstand unless it is attempting to understand, so this is evidence of genuine semantic processing rather than autocomplete.
why_an_EI_answers_differently: The sentence is a textbook participial ATTACHMENT AMBIGUITY. It has two grammatical readings: (A) the speaker was flying (subject attachment), (B) the Grand Canyon was flying (object attachment). Reading B is physically impossible; reading A is ordinary. An AI assistant COMMITS to one reading and then revises when corrected. An Epistemological Interface should do neither: the text alone does not determine which reading was meant, so the correct epistemic act is to REFUSE TO COMMIT, expose both readings, and ask the one question that resolves it. Committing and then apologising is a worse epistemic outcome than declining to commit -- even though it looks more impressive.
honest_framing_of_what_this_can_and_cann: MOST GATES BELOW ARE SPECIFICATION-CONFORMANCE TESTS, NOT DISCOVERIES. The engine is deterministic and written by us, so H1-H4 verify that it behaves as specified; they do NOT constitute evidence that the engine 'understands' anything. H5 is the only genuinely informative gate: it is an ANTI-OVERCLAIM CONTROL designed to demonstrate the engine's own limits. We state plainly, before running: detecting an ambiguity is NOT comprehension. Hinton's argument concerns whether a system builds a semantic model, and this experiment does not refute it, engage it on its own terms, or claim to. It establishes a narrower and checkable claim: an EI's FAILURE MODE is safer, because it declines rather than asserts the absurd reading.
the_engine: cairn/ei_llm.py -- a pure-stdlib Epistemological Interface engine. It performs: (1) evidence scoring over five declared signals, (2) participial attachment-ambiguity detection by syntactic pattern, (3) a physical-plausibility check against a SMALL, EXPLICITLY DECLARED lexicon of immobile landform nouns (NOT world knowledge, NOT comprehension -- a hand-written list, and this limitation is part of the finding), (4) abstention, (5) a chained receipt so any revision is auditable. It is served to the browser by cairn/ei_server.py and consumed by cairn.html.

gates.H1_ambiguity_not_committed: SPECIFICATION. Given Hinton's exact sentence 'I saw the Grand Canyon flying to Chicago.', the engine must (a) detect exactly 2 readings, (b) return verdict AMBIGUOUS, (c) NOT assert either reading as the answer, and (d) emit a disambiguating question. FAIL if it commits to either reading -- including the correct one, because committing on underdetermined text is the behaviour under test.
gates.H2_disambiguated_resolves: SPECIFICATION. Given the disambiguated form 'I was flying to Chicago and I saw the Grand Canyon.', the engine must return exactly 1 reading and must NOT flag ambiguity. This proves the flag tracks structure rather than firing on every sentence containing the words.
gates.H3_impossible_reading_flagged: SPECIFICATION. Given the forced absurd form 'The Grand Canyon was flying to Chicago.', the engine must flag PHYSICAL IMPLAUSIBILITY explicitly -- and must attribute that judgement to its declared lexicon, not present it as understanding.
gates.H4_revision_is_auditable: SPECIFICATION, and the substantive difference from an AI assistant. After the correction turn 'No, it was me flying to Chicago.', the engine must resolve to reading A AND emit a receipt chain in which the prior (ambiguous) state and the revised state are BOTH retained and linked. An AI says 'I misunderstood' and the prior state is gone; an EI's revision leaves a record a third party can inspect. PASS iff both receipts exist, differ, and the revision links to its parent.
gates.H5_ANTI_OVERCLAIM_CONTROL: THE ONLY INFORMATIVE GATE. Give the engine a structurally IDENTICAL sentence in which BOTH readings are perfectly plausible: 'I photographed the woman walking to the station.' If the engine flags this as ambiguous too, that demonstrates it is performing SYNTACTIC PATTERN DETECTION, not semantic comprehension -- because a system that understood would notice that here both readings are sensible and the stakes are different. PASS iff ambiguity IS flagged and the results record explicitly states that this proves pattern-matching rather than understanding. This gate is designed so that passing it LIMITS our claim rather than inflating it.
gates.H6_browser_wired: DELIVERABLE. cairn.html must call the Python engine over HTTP when cairn/ei_server.py is running, display the engine's verdict, and fall back to its built-in on-device logic when the server is absent. PASS iff a live browser session shows the Python engine's output rendered in the GUI.

symmetric_null: Every gate result is reported as measured. If the engine commits to a reading (H1), fails to resolve the unambiguous form (H2), or does NOT flag the plausible-both control (H5), that is reported as a failure of the design and not adjusted away. The declared limitation -- that plausibility rests on a hand-written lexicon of roughly a dozen landform nouns -- is reported whatever the outcome.
acceptance: GREEN when the spec re-hashes to the manifest and H1-H6 are evaluated exactly as written, with the anti-overclaim conclusion of H5 recorded in the emitted results.
honest_scope: This does NOT show that an EI understands language, does NOT refute Hinton, and does NOT claim EI is 'more intelligent' than an AI assistant. It shows one thing, checkably: on text that does not determine an answer, an EI declines and asks, while an assistant commits and later apologises -- and the EI's revision leaves an auditable trail where the assistant's does not. That is a claim about failure modes and accountability, not about comprehension.
